stories.title: The Bank of England's November Financial Stability Report (26 Nov) completes its bank capital review: the PRA will consult on lower minimum requirements for domestic lending, cutting Tier 1 requirements for major UK banks by about 50 basis points of risk-weighted assets in normal times, with system-wide requirements consistent with a new benchmark of about 13% and the neutral CCyB kept at 2%. The FPC also warns that AI-related financing (hyperscaler bonds above $305bn in 2026, about 8% of global investment-grade issuance, plus private credit and circular vendor financing) is deepening interconnections, and that frontier AI agents, open-weight models and quantum computing are raising cyber and operational risk
stories.h: Bank of England cuts UK bank capital requirements and warns AI borrowing links risks together
stories.sub: Tier 1 needs fall by about 0.5 points of risk-weighted assets; hyperscaler bonds pass $305bn this year
stories.ticker: BoE completes capital review: major UK banks' Tier 1 needs cut ~50bp of RWAs; FPC flags $305bn+ AI bond wave
stories.body:
The Bank of England's Financial Policy Committee published its November Financial Stability Report on 26 Nov and closed its review of bank capital. The PRA will consult on lower minimum requirements for domestic lending, which together with earlier changes cut Tier 1 capital requirements for major UK banks by about 50 basis points of risk-weighted assets in normal times, with further relief in stress scenarios. System-wide requirements will sit at the FPC's updated benchmark of around 13%, and the neutral countercyclical buffer stays at 2%. The FPC says going much further 'would risk financial instability'.

The same report warns that AI-related financing now spans equities, public bonds, private credit and 'circular' vendor-financing deals: hyperscaler bond issuance is set to exceed $305bn in 2026, about 8% of global investment-grade issuance. It says frontier AI agents and open-weight models make cyber and operational risk a more prominent threat, and asks firms to speed up quantum-safe cryptography.

So what: UK lenders get room to lend or return capital, but supervisors want to see where AI-linked exposures sit and how fast banks can recover from cyber incidents; expect questions on both in 2027 reviews.
stories.chip: Checked on the Bank of England's November 2026 Financial Stability Report page (opened)
src: Bank of England: Financial Stability Report, November 2026
FT: BoE to cut capital requirements for banks as it warns of AI risks
WSJ: BoE warns scale and breadth of AI financing poses threat to financial stability
stories.brief:
Twice a year the Bank of England's Financial Policy Committee sets out the risks to the UK financial system. This report did two things at once. It finished a review the government wanted, aimed at freeing banks to lend more: minimum requirements tied to domestic lending will fall, so the biggest UK banks need roughly half a percentage point less Tier 1 capital against their risk-weighted assets, and the committee's overall benchmark settles at about 13%. It also drew a line: cutting much further would weaken banks' ability to absorb shocks.

The risk section is where AI comes in. Borrowing to build data centres is growing fast and spreading across bonds, private credit and complex vendor-financing loops, which makes it harder to see who ultimately holds the risk. The committee also says more capable AI agents and open-weight models raise the bar for cyber defence, and that the shift to quantum-resistant cryptography should start now.
facts: FSR closes the capital review; Tier 1 requirements for major UK banks fall by ~50bp of RWAs
Hyperscaler bonds >$305bn in 2026, ~8% of global IG issuance
Frontier AI agents and open-weight models raise cyber risk; start quantum-safe migration
PRA consultation on the lower domestic-lending requirements

stories.short: The Bank of England finished its capital review: major UK banks' Tier 1 requirements fall by about half a percentage point of risk-weighted assets, with an overall benchmark near 13%. It also warned that AI borrowing, including over $305 billion of hyperscaler bonds this year, ties risks together, and that AI agents raise cyber risk.

stories.title: SAP confirms (27 Nov) a cybersecurity incident after Der Spiegel reported that hackers obtained employees' authentication tokens for SAP's GitHub-hosted development environment, letting them copy and alter source code; SAP restricted GitHub access, halted automated development pipelines and replaced the keys used to sign its software (internal response 'Project Granite', per Handelsblatt)
stories.h: SAP confirms hackers got into its GitHub development systems; signing keys replaced
stories.ticker: SAP confirms incident: attackers used staff GitHub tokens to reach source code; signing keys rotated
stories.body:
SAP confirmed on Friday that it is investigating a cyber incident after Der Spiegel reported that attackers obtained employees' authentication tokens for SAP's development environment on GitHub, which let them copy and modify source code. According to The Record, SAP has restricted GitHub access, halted automated development processes and replaced the digital keys it uses to prove its software is genuine. Handelsblatt says the response is code-named 'Project Granite'. SAP says it moved immediately to protect customers; it has not said whether any shipped code was altered.

So what: SAP runs core ledgers, payroll and treasury at most large banks. Ask SAP whether any patches or packages were signed with the old keys, and check that your update channels pin the new ones.
stories.chip: Checked on The Record, SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer (opened); Der Spiegel report is paywalled
src: The Record: SAP confirms cyber incident amid reports of source code breach
SecurityWeek: SAP confirms cyberattack, source code reportedly compromised
BleepingComputer: SAP confirms incident after suspicious GitHub activity
stories.short: SAP confirmed a cyber incident after reports that attackers stole staff GitHub tokens and could copy and change its source code. SAP restricted GitHub, paused automated builds and replaced its software-signing keys. It has not said whether any shipped code was altered, which matters to the many banks running SAP.

stories.title: Hackers breached the US Air Force's Cloud One platform, Reuters reports (27 Nov): the intrusion, found within the past month during an upgrade, used an unidentified software vulnerability and disrupted migrations and updates; Cloud One pools Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Google clouds and hosts systems including Cloud-Based Command and Control (North American air-defence radar feeds) and the Theater Integrated Combat Munitions System; it follows breaches at FinCEN, the FBI's NCIC and a CIA OSINT system
stories.h: Hackers breached the US Air Force cloud that runs air-defence and munitions systems
stories.ticker: Reuters: US Air Force Cloud One breached via unknown flaw; hosts air-defence and munitions apps
stories.body:
Attackers got into Cloud One, the US Air Force's shared cloud platform, by exploiting an unidentified software vulnerability, Reuters reports. The breach was found within the past month during an upgrade and disrupted application migrations and software updates. Cloud One, launched in 2017, pools Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Google clouds; per Decrypt it hosts the Air Force's Cloud-Based Command and Control (air-defence radar feeds across North America) and a system that tracks munitions at more than 200 bases. The Air Force declined to comment. It is the fourth reported US federal breach in about two weeks, after FinCEN, the FBI's NCIC database and a CIA open-source intelligence system.

So what: no attribution yet, but a run of federal breaches through shared platforms is exactly the concentration risk the Bank of England flagged the same week; expect new CISA directives.

Decrypt: hackers hit Air Force cloud system running air-defence and munitions data

stories.short: Reuters reports hackers breached Cloud One, the US Air Force's shared cloud built on Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Google, through an unknown software flaw. It hosts air-defence radar and munitions-tracking systems. It is the fourth reported US federal breach in about two weeks, after FinCEN, the FBI and the CIA. No attribution yet.

stories.title: Euro zone governments pick Pablo Hernández de Cos, the former Bank of Spain governor and current BIS general manager, as the next ECB president (26-27 Nov), after his only rival Klaas Knot congratulated him; he takes over when Christine Lagarde leaves early in 2027 (7 Feb, Reuters via FintechNews) and chairs his first policy meeting on 18 March; Reuters reads the choice as policy continuity and readiness to fight any sovereign-debt stress
stories.h: Pablo Hernández de Cos, head of the BIS, will run the ECB from February
stories.ticker: Euro zone picks BIS chief Pablo Hernández de Cos as next ECB president; first meeting 18 March
stories.body:
Euro zone countries have chosen Pablo Hernández de Cos, 55, the BIS general manager and former governor of the Bank of Spain, to succeed Christine Lagarde as ECB president. The race ended on 26 Nov when Dutch rival Klaas Knot congratulated him. Reuters, cited by FintechNews, says Lagarde steps down early on 7 Feb 2027 and de Cos chairs his first rate meeting on 18 March; the deal also fills two Executive Board seats for Germany and France. He ran Spain's central bank through the Covid shock and the 2022-23 rate rises and chaired the Basel Committee.

So what: a Basel veteran at the ECB means continuity on rates and a supervisor who knows the bank-capital rules by heart; markets read him as willing to backstop sovereign debt, which matters with France's rating outlook now negative.
stories.chip: Checked on Central Banking and FintechNews Switzerland (opened), the latter citing Reuters
src: Central Banking: De Cos to take over as ECB president
FintechNews CH: Pablo Hernández de Cos named next ECB president
stories.short: Euro zone governments picked Pablo Hernández de Cos, head of the BIS and former Bank of Spain governor, to replace Christine Lagarde at the ECB. Reuters says he takes over on 7 February and chairs his first rate meeting on 18 March. Markets expect continuity and a firm hand on bank rules.

stories.title: OpenAI files counterclaims against Apple in California federal court (27 Nov, FT/Reuters), alleging Apple stole its trade secrets by rehiring an employee who spent six months at OpenAI with access to device plans and its hardware roadmap, 'coerced and threatened' shared suppliers, and encouraged staff to keep corporate files on personal devices; it answers Apple's July lawsuit over ex-Apple designers who joined io/OpenAI
stories.h: OpenAI countersues Apple, accusing it of stealing device secrets and pressuring suppliers
stories.ticker: OpenAI countersues Apple: alleges theft of device roadmap and 'coercing' shared suppliers
stories.body:
OpenAI filed counterclaims against Apple in California federal court, the FT and Reuters report. It says Apple gained confidential information by rehiring an employee who had spent six months at OpenAI with access to a new device and its hardware roadmap, and that Apple is 'coercing and threatening' suppliers that also work with OpenAI. OpenAI says its devices threaten to 'outcompete Apple on what Apple views as its own turf'. The filing answers Apple's July suit against OpenAI, io Products and two former Apple designers. Apple said in October its investigation had found no OpenAI files.

So what: the fight is now about access to the Asian supply chain for AI devices, not just hiring; component makers serving both firms may face discovery and pressure to pick sides.

stories.short: OpenAI countersued Apple in California, saying Apple stole its device secrets by rehiring an employee who had seen its hardware roadmap, and pressured suppliers that work with both companies. It answers Apple's July lawsuit over designers who joined OpenAI. Apple had said it found no OpenAI files.

stories.title: US Central Command says (27 Nov) aircraft struck the stern of the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman on 26 Nov after it left Bandar Abbas, disabling it as it tried to run the US blockade of Iranian ports (reimposed in July); an adviser to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei vows to keep Hormuz shut and break the embargo; Iranian-made drones hit Kuwaiti military sites on 26 Nov, killing two Italian Rheinmetall technicians, which Iran denies
stories.h: US disables a ship running its Iran blockade; drones kill two Italians in Kuwait
stories.ticker: CENTCOM disables Pacific Archer leaving Bandar Abbas; drones kill two Italians at Kuwait base
stories.body:
US aircraft struck the Palau-flagged Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman after it sailed from Bandar Abbas, disabling its propulsion without hurting the crew, US Central Command said; it was trying to run the naval blockade of Iranian ports the US reimposed in July. An adviser to Iran's Supreme Leader said Tehran would keep the Strait of Hormuz shut and break the embargo. Separately, Iranian-made drones hit Kuwaiti military installations on Thursday, killing two Italian technicians from Rheinmetall, Italy and Kuwait said; Iran's foreign minister denied involvement. Iran has stepped up attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain this week.

So what: Hormuz stays effectively closed going into Sunday's OPEC+ meeting, keeping oil near $90 and feeding the energy-driven inflation the Bank of England and Fed are worried about.

src: CNA (Reuters): US disables ship trying to leave Iran
The Hindu: two Italians killed in drone attack in Kuwait
stories.short: US Central Command said its aircraft disabled the Pacific Archer as it tried to leave Iran through the US blockade. Iran vowed to keep the Strait of Hormuz shut. Drones that Italy and Kuwait say were Iranian killed two Italian technicians at a Kuwaiti base; Iran denies it.

stories.title: The RBI cuts banks' minimum daily CRR maintenance back to 90% from 99% from 1 Dec (27 Nov) as system liquidity swings to a deficit of Rs 47,641 crore on 26 Nov (from an Rs 11 trillion surplus in September), the overall CRR staying at 3%; it also issues final directions letting banks place temporary debit holds on suspected money-mule accounts under a uniform SOP (from 1 July 2027 or earlier), lets white-label ATM operators source cash from any bank or RBI issue offices, and consolidates 17 ATM/PoS cash-withdrawal circulars
stories.h: RBI eases daily cash-reserve rule as liquidity turns tight, and sets money-mule account holds
stories.ticker: RBI: daily CRR minimum back to 90% from 1 Dec; banks get SOP to freeze suspected mule accounts
stories.body:
The RBI reversed its October tightening: from 1 Dec banks need to hold only 90% of required cash reserves on any day, not 99%, with the overall CRR unchanged at 3%. Mint says system liquidity has swung from a surplus of about Rs 11 trillion in mid-September to a deficit of Rs 47,641 crore on 26 Nov, as forex intervention and government cash balances drained funds. The same day the RBI issued final directions giving banks a standard procedure to put temporary debit holds on accounts suspected of money-mule activity, coordinated with police, effective 1 July 2027 (earlier if a bank chooses). It also let white-label ATM operators buy cash from any bank, or directly from RBI issue offices, and merged 17 ATM and PoS cash-withdrawal circulars.

So what: the CRR change frees short-term funding for treasuries into year-end; the mule-account SOP gives fraud teams legal cover to freeze first, but they must build the release process with law enforcement.
stories.chip: Checked on the RBI press release on mule-account directions (opened), plus Mint and ET BFSI (opened)

stories.short: India's central bank cut the daily cash-reserve minimum back to 90% from 99% from 1 December, as banking liquidity slipped into a deficit of about Rs 47,600 crore. It also gave banks a standard way to freeze suspected money-mule accounts from July 2027, and let white-label ATM firms buy cash from any bank.

stories.title: US stocks rebound in the shortened Black Friday session (27 Nov): the Nasdaq Composite rises 2.3% to 24,129.50, the S&P 500 1.6% to 7,297.49 and the Dow 1.2% to 50,774.94 (Yahoo Finance data); Anthropic jumps 11% to $91.88, back above its $83 IPO price, ahead of a first lock-up release of up to 303m shares on 15 Dec; Nvidia edges up 0.8% to $150.49; the 10-year yield rises to 4.94% and Brent falls to $90.84 before Sunday's OPEC+ meeting
stories.h: US tech stocks bounce 2.3% on Black Friday; Anthropic jumps 11% above its IPO price
stories.body:
After Wednesday's near-bear-market scare, US stocks rallied in Friday's short post-Thanksgiving session: the Nasdaq rose 2.3% to 24,129.50, the S&P 500 1.6% to 7,297.49 and the Dow 1.2% to 50,774.94. Anthropic gained about 11% to $91.88, back above its $83 IPO price; Crypto Briefing notes up to 303m shares (174m Class A, 129m Class N) become sellable on 15 Dec. Nvidia added 0.8% to $150.49. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.94%, and Brent fell to $90.84 ahead of OPEC+ talks.

So what: one strong half-day does not undo November's AI sell-off; next week's US jobs data and the 15 Dec Anthropic unlock are the tests, with a Fed hike still priced for 10 Dec.

stories.title: A researcher publishes (27 Nov) an unpatched zero-day exploit chain for Cacti, the open-source network monitoring tool, that takes an unauthenticated HTTP session to command execution in four requests, with a public proof-of-concept and video ('Sad Girls 0day Club' repo); Cacti servers often store SNMP credentials for routers, switches and firewalls; no patch yet
stories.h: Unpatched Cacti flaw with public exploit lets anyone run commands on monitoring servers
stories.ticker: Cacti zero-day with public PoC: unauthenticated RCE in four requests; no patch yet
stories.body:
A researcher disclosed an unpatched flaw in Cacti, the open-source tool many IT teams use to graph servers, routers and firewalls, and published a working exploit: from an unauthenticated web session to command execution in four requests, BleepingComputer reports. Because Cacti often stores the SNMP credentials it uses to poll network gear, a compromised server can open the way to the rest of the network. No fix has been released.

So what: take Cacti web interfaces off any network an attacker could reach today and rotate the stored SNMP credentials; with public code, scanning will start within days.
stories.chip: Checked on BleepingComputer (opened); no vendor advisory yet
src: BleepingComputer: unpatched Cacti zero-day with public PoC
stories.short: A researcher published a working exploit for an unpatched flaw in Cacti, a widely used network-monitoring tool, that runs commands on the server without logging in. Cacti often stores credentials for routers and firewalls. There is no patch yet, so cutting off access to Cacti's web interface is the stopgap.

stat.label: requests from no login to running commands

stories.title: InfoHawk reports (27 Nov) a card-skimming script that used WebRTC data channels to load and exfiltrate card details was planted on the online stores of Lascana, Samsonite, American Tourister, Revolve and FWRD in the week before Black Friday; it saw a test card sent to a third party on Lascana; Revolve says it fixed the issue on its mobile sites on 25 Nov; the number of victims is unknown
stories.h: Black Friday card skimmer hid in WebRTC on Samsonite, Revolve and three other stores
stories.ticker: WebRTC card skimmer found on Samsonite, Revolve, FWRD, Lascana, American Tourister before Black Friday
stories.body:
Security firm InfoHawk found a card-skimming script on the online stores of Lascana, Samsonite, American Tourister, Revolve and FWRD in the week before Black Friday. The script used WebRTC, the browser technology behind video calls, both to load itself and to send card details out, because many security tools do not watch that channel. InfoHawk saw its test card sent to a third party on Lascana. Revolve says it fixed the issue on its mobile and tablet sites the day it was told (25 Nov). How many shoppers were hit is unknown.

So what: issuers should watch for card-not-present fraud on cards used at these merchants this month; merchants should add WebRTC to their content-security policies.
stories.chip: Checked on InfoHawk's research post (opened), which quotes Revolve's statement
src: InfoHawk: card skimming scripts using WebRTC found on popular shopping sites
stories.short: Researchers at InfoHawk found a card skimmer on the Samsonite, American Tourister, Revolve, FWRD and Lascana online stores before Black Friday. It hid in WebRTC, the video-call channel many security tools ignore, and sent a test card to a third party. Revolve says it fixed its sites on 25 November; victim numbers are unknown.

stories.title: Sber's GigaChat team (ai-sage on Hugging Face) releases GigaChat 4 open weights under MIT (repo created 20 Nov, updated 27 Nov): a 708B-parameter mixture-of-experts with 41B active, hybrid Gated DeltaNet linear attention plus DeepSeek Sparse Attention, a 1M-token context and both instant and reasoning modes in one model; its card reports 80.9 on SWE-bench Verified in reasoning mode; FP8, BF16, GGUF, base and intermediate checkpoints, plus a 37B-A4B small model
stories.h: Russia's Sber releases GigaChat 4, a 708B open model with a million-token context
stories.cat: AI models & labs · open models · 27 Nov
stories.ticker: GigaChat 4 open weights (MIT): 708B MoE, 41B active, 1M context; card claims 80.9 SWE-bench Verified
stories.body:
The GigaChat team at Russia's largest bank, Sber, has published GigaChat 4 on Hugging Face under the MIT licence: 708B parameters, 41B active per token, mixing linear attention (Gated DeltaNet) with DeepSeek-style sparse attention for a 1M-token context, and offering instant and reasoning modes in one model. Its own evaluation table reports 80.9 on SWE-bench Verified in reasoning mode, near the top open models it compares against. It ships FP8, BF16 and GGUF weights, the base model and intermediate training checkpoints, and a small 37B-A4B sibling. Benchmarks are the team's own.

So what: a bank-built model at the open frontier, with checkpoints researchers can study; Western banks will not deploy a Russian model, but it shows how far in-house bank AI can go.
stories.chip: Checked on the Hugging Face model card and API (licence, size, dates; opened); benchmarks are self-reported
stories.short: Sber's GigaChat team released GigaChat 4 under the MIT licence: a 708-billion-parameter model that uses 41 billion per token, reads up to a million tokens and switches between quick and reasoning modes. Its own tests score 80.9 on SWE-bench Verified. Weights, base model and training checkpoints are all public.

stories.title: Lloyds Bank and Bank of Scotland customers cannot log in or move money on the morning of Friday 27 Nov, a payday and Black Friday; Bank of Scotland's status page acknowledges app and online banking problems; earlier in 2026 a botched overnight update at Lloyds Banking Group exposed transactions to almost 448,000 app users
stories.h: Lloyds and Bank of Scotland apps fail on payday and Black Friday
stories.ticker: Lloyds and Bank of Scotland app and online banking down on Friday morning (payday)
stories.body:
Lloyds Bank and Bank of Scotland customers reported they could not access online banking or transfer money on Friday morning, a payday that was also Black Friday; Bank of Scotland's service status page confirmed app and online problems, The Register reports. Lloyds Banking Group had a separate incident earlier this year when a software update exposed other customers' transactions to almost 448,000 app users.

So what: the UK's biggest retail bank failing on a peak day is the kind of incident the Bank of England's resilience warnings are about; expect the FCA to ask for the root cause.
stories.chip: Checked on The Register (opened)

stories.h: S&P moves France's credit outlook to negative
stories.ticker: S&P revises France rating outlook to negative from stable
stories.body:
S&P cut the outlook on France's credit rating to negative from stable on Friday, according to WSJ, FT and France 24 headlines; we could not open the reports for the rating level or the reasons. The Bank of England's report this week singled out France as a country where fiscal and political uncertainty have pushed bond yields up.

So what: a downgrade would raise funding costs for French banks and pressure the ECB's incoming president early.

stories.title: Los Angeles Unified, the second-largest US school district, 'temporarily suspends' Google's AI Overviews on student devices (AP, 27 Nov), the largest district yet to work around Google's stance that schools turning off AI must give up search; Google had said it would switch off Gemini and search for K-12 students by default, leaving schools to opt in
stories.h: Los Angeles schools switch off Google's AI Overviews on student laptops
stories.ticker: LA Unified suspends Google AI Overviews on student devices as Google ties search to AI
stories.body:
Los Angeles Unified, the second-largest US school district, has 'temporarily suspended' Google's AI Overviews on student devices to keep search 'age-appropriate and safe', the AP reports. Google has said schools that switch AI off entirely lose search too, and earlier this month made Gemini and search off by default for K-12 students; some districts are building workarounds or weighing other search engines.

So what: the first big institutional customer pushing back on AI-only search; watch whether Google offers a plain-search option for education.

stories.title: pCloud confirms (27 Nov) a cyberattack on its pCloud Pass password manager, 'quickly contained', after users worldwide got alerts that an unknown device named 'pd' connected to their accounts from a Luxembourg IP that users say belongs to pCloud, even with 2FA on, and some who never used Pass were alerted
stories.h: pCloud confirms its password manager was hacked after strange login alerts
stories.ticker: pCloud confirms attack on pCloud Pass password manager; users saw unknown device logins despite 2FA
stories.body:
pCloud confirmed its pCloud Pass password manager was attacked, saying it was quickly contained, after customers worldwide received alerts that an unknown device called 'pd' had connected to their accounts, some with two-factor authentication on, BleepingComputer reports. Users say the IP address belongs to pCloud's own infrastructure.

So what: the second password-manager breach this week after 1Password; anyone using pCloud Pass should rotate high-value passwords now.
stories.chip: Checked on BleepingComputer (opened)
src: BleepingComputer: pCloud confirms password manager hack

stories.title: The North Korea-linked PolinRider campaign has compromised more than 7,600 GitHub repositories since perhaps February 2025, The Hacker News reports (26 Nov); a newer Python loader that runs when developers clone and execute projects was found in 375 public repos across 260 accounts; no sign it reached PyPI or npm
stories.h: North Korea-linked PolinRider poisoned more than 7,600 GitHub repositories
stories.ticker: PolinRider: 7,600+ GitHub repos compromised; Python loader found in 375 repos
stories.body:
The PolinRider campaign, linked to North Korea, has compromised more than 7,600 GitHub repositories, possibly since February 2025, The Hacker News reports. Its latest trick is a Python loader planted in 375 public repositories belonging to 260 accounts that runs when developers clone and run or import a project. There is no evidence it was spread through PyPI or npm.

So what: with SAP and 1Password both breached through GitHub this week, treat developer accounts and cloned code as an attack surface.
stories.chip: Checked on The Hacker News (opened)
src: The Hacker News: PolinRider poisons over 7,600 GitHub repositories

stories.title: Researchers show (27 Nov) AMD fTPM and Winbond SPI-flash flaws that let an attacker with physical access brute-force BitLocker PINs, cutting a six-digit PIN from about 19 years to about 20 days; Winbond-based machines cannot be fixed without new hardware, AMD PCs need new BIOS
stories.h: AMD and Winbond flaws cut BitLocker PIN cracking from 19 years to 20 days
stories.ticker: AMD/Winbond flaws: stolen-laptop BitLocker PIN brute force drops to ~20 days
stories.body:
Flaws in AMD's firmware TPM and in Winbond flash chips let someone who has stolen a laptop brute-force its BitLocker PIN, cutting a six-digit PIN from roughly 19 years to about 20 days, Tom's Hardware reports. Machines using affected Winbond chips cannot be fixed without new hardware; AMD systems will need BIOS updates.

So what: banks relying on TPM-plus-PIN for laptop encryption should move to longer PINs or startup keys on affected models.
stories.chip: Checked on Tom's Hardware (opened); vendor advisories not yet checked
src: Tom's Hardware: AMD and Winbond vulnerabilities let attackers brute-force BitLocker PINs

stories.title: SAP is weighing at least 10,000 job cuts, about 9% of its 110,000-plus staff, in an AI-driven restructuring, Bloomberg reports (26 Nov); German staff, about a quarter of the workforce, have a job guarantee to 2028; SAP says only that it reviews its structure continuously
stories.h: SAP weighs at least 10,000 job cuts as it reorganises around AI
stories.ticker: Bloomberg: SAP weighs 10,000+ job cuts (~9% of staff) in AI overhaul
stories.body:
SAP is considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs, about 9% of its workforce, as CEO Christian Klein builds AI into its products, Bloomberg reports. Staff in Germany, a quarter of the total, are protected by a job guarantee until 2028. SAP declined to comment beyond saying it reviews its organisation continuously.

So what: another big software employer cutting staff in the name of AI, in the same week it disclosed a breach of its developer systems.
stories.chip: Checked on SiliconANGLE and The Decoder (opened), citing Bloomberg
src: SiliconANGLE: SAP reportedly plans to lay off 10,000+ employees
The Decoder: SAP plans to cut at least 10,000 jobs

stories.title: TrueLayer and Papa Johns complete a pilot (in the FCA's Supercharged Sandbox) in which Papa Johns' AI agent took an order and paid by bank using Lloyds' and NatWest's variable recurring payment APIs, with a bank-set spending cap the agent cannot exceed and approval in the customer's bank app, so no card details were shared
stories.h: TrueLayer and Papa Johns test an AI agent paying by bank with a hard spending cap
stories.ticker: TrueLayer x Papa Johns: AI agent pays via Lloyds/NatWest VRP with bank-set cap
stories.body:
TrueLayer and Papa Johns ran a pilot in the FCA's Supercharged Sandbox where the pizza chain's AI assistant took an order and paid from the customer's linked bank account using Lloyds and NatWest variable recurring payment APIs. The customer set a spending limit with their bank that the agent cannot exceed and approved the mandate in their banking app, so no card or password went to the agent, PYMNTS reports.

So what: a working model for agent payments where the bank, not the card network, holds the guardrail; UK banks with VRP APIs have a product to sell.
stories.chip: Checked on PYMNTS (opened), based on the companies' release
src: PYMNTS: TrueLayer and Papa Johns pit pay by bank against cards in agentic commerce

stories.title: Russia's second-largest bank VTB lets brokerage clients trade crypto in its 'My Investments' app from 27 Nov, over the counter and only for qualified investors who pass a new Bank of Russia-mandated test, with VTB holding the assets on Russian infrastructure in a separate digital depository account
stories.h: Russia's VTB opens bitcoin trading for qualified investors
stories.ticker: VTB opens OTC crypto trading for qualified investors from 27 Nov
stories.body:
VTB, Russia's second-largest bank, opened crypto trading in its investment app on 27 Nov, Bitcoin Magazine reports. Trades are over the counter, limited to qualified investors who also pass a new test, and VTB holds the coins itself in a separate digital depository account.

So what: a sanctioned state bank offering bitcoin is another channel Western compliance teams will need to screen for.
stories.chip: Checked on Bitcoin Magazine (opened)
src: Bitcoin Magazine: Russia's VTB opens bitcoin trading

stories.title: OPEC+ ministers meet on Sunday 29 Nov to set 2027 quotas and maximum capacity levels for each member, with little visibility on the US war with Iran; reports expect targets held steady, Iraq is pushing for a higher quota, and Brent settled at $90.84 on Friday
stories.h: OPEC+ meets Sunday to set 2027 quotas with Hormuz still shut
stories.ticker: OPEC+ meets Sunday on 2027 quotas and capacity; Brent $90.84
stories.body:
OPEC+ meets on Sunday to set 2027 output quotas and, for the first time, maximum capacity levels for each member that will anchor future quotas, the Japan Times (AFP) reports; the Economic Times says targets are expected to stay steady, while Iraq pushes for more. Brent settled at $90.84 on Friday.

So what: with Hormuz shut, the capacity numbers matter more than the quotas for where oil goes in 2027.
stories.chip: Checked on the Japan Times and the Economic Times (opened); Brent from Yahoo Finance data
src: Japan Times: OPEC+ facing tricky talks on 2027 output and capacity
Economic Times: OPEC+ set to keep production targets steady

stories.title: Spain holds a snap general election on Sunday 29 Nov; polls before the five-day publication ban show an advantage for a PP-Vox coalition led by Alberto Núñez Feijóo, while Pedro Sánchez says internal data point to a PSOE win with left-wing allies
stories.h: Spain votes Sunday; polls favour a PP-Vox coalition over Sánchez
stories.ticker: Spain votes Sunday: polls favour PP-Vox; Sánchez bets on left surge
stories.body:
Spain holds a snap general election on Sunday. Nearly all polls before the legal blackout showed a lead for a coalition of the conservative PP under Alberto Núñez Feijóo and the far-right Vox; Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez says internal data show his Socialists winning the most votes, Al Jazeera reports. Housing and immigration dominate.

So what: a PP-Vox government would be the euro zone's fourth-largest economy turning right weeks before a Spaniard takes over the ECB.
stories.chip: Checked on Al Jazeera (opened)
src: Al Jazeera: Sánchez bets on left-wing surge to defy polls

stories.title: Taiwan votes on Saturday 28 Nov in local elections, with the Taipei mayoral race watched most closely, alongside a referendum on whether to bring back nuclear power 18 months after its last reactor shut, its fourth nuclear vote in eight years, framed around power for AI chipmaking; China tested new Taiwan landing tactics in coastal drills this week
stories.h: Taiwan votes on mayors and on bringing back nuclear power
stories.ticker: Taiwan local elections and nuclear referendum today; results due tonight
stories.body:
Taiwan elects thousands of local officials on Saturday, with all eyes on the Taipei mayor race (Nikkei Asia), and votes in a referendum on reviving nuclear power, 18 months after its last reactor shut, Al Jazeera reports; the debate is about electricity for chip fabs and AI data centres. China ran coastal drills testing new landing tactics this week (Japan Times). Results come tonight Taiwan time.

So what: a yes vote would change the power outlook for TSMC's island fabs.
stories.chip: Checked on Al Jazeera and Nikkei Asia (opened); results not yet in
src: Al Jazeera: Will Taiwan vote to revive nuclear power?
Nikkei Asia: Taiwan votes with all eyes on Taipei mayor races
Japan Times: Chinese military tests new Taiwan landing tactics

stories.title: Xpeng says at its AI Day it will start mass-producing its Iron humanoid robot in January 2027, deploy it first as a store assistant, target tens of thousands of sales next year and could reach homes in one to two years at about the price of one of its cars (co-president Brian Gu)
stories.h: Xpeng will mass-produce its Iron humanoid from January
stories.ticker: Xpeng: Iron humanoid mass production from Jan 2027; tens of thousands targeted
stories.body:
Chinese EV maker Xpeng will start mass-producing its Iron humanoid in January, training it first as a store assistant, TNW reports. Co-president Brian Gu says it could be in homes in one to two years at roughly the price of an Xpeng car, with tens of thousands of sales targeted for 2027.

So what: Chinese carmakers are turning humanoids into a volume product; Goldman's new sell rating on Unitree shows investors doubt the pricing.
stories.chip: Checked on TNW (opened)
src: TNW: Xpeng says its Iron humanoid could be doing chores in one or two years

stories.title: OpenAI says (26 Nov) it fixed a billing bug that had under-counted GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage, so ChatGPT and Codex users will hit limits 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol than last week; users can reset exhausted limits once in Settings
stories.h: OpenAI fixes a billing bug, so GPT-6.2 users hit limits 40% sooner
stories.ticker: OpenAI: GPT-6.2 Astra limits reached 40% faster, Sol 25%, after billing-bug fix
stories.body:
OpenAI's Tibo Sottiaux said a bug had wrongly discounted GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage; with it fixed, users reach limits 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol than last week, BleepingComputer reports. Users can reset exhausted limits under Settings > Usage. A Hacker News thread (507 points) reads it as cost control.

So what: plan seats on real usage, not launch-week allowances.
stories.chip: Checked on BleepingComputer (opened), quoting OpenAI's post on X
src: BleepingComputer: GPT-6.2 Astra will hit usage limits 40% faster

stories.title: A Tencent-led team publishes in Nature an AI method for designing dual-target therapeutic peptides, with candidates for obesity and cancer, per SCMP and Pandaily headlines (27 Nov)
stories.h: Tencent's AI designs dual-target peptides for obesity and cancer, in Nature
stories.ticker: Tencent-led Nature paper: AI-designed dual-target peptides for obesity and cancer
stories.body:
A team led by Tencent's AI lab has a paper in Nature on AI-designed peptides that hit two drug targets at once, with candidates for obesity and cancer, SCMP and Pandaily report. We could not open either report, so results and trial status are unchecked.

So what: Chinese tech groups are now publishing drug-design work at the top journals.
stories.chip: SCMP and Pandaily headlines only (pages blocked or empty)
src: SCMP: Tencent makes AI drug discovery breakthrough with Nature paper
Pandaily: Tencent lab leads Nature paper on AI-designed dual-target peptides

stories.title: Swiss regulator FINMA approves UBS's 2025 recovery plan, the first approval since the Credit Suisse takeover, and finds its preferred resolution strategy (a bail-in) can be carried out as the integration advances (26 Nov)
stories.h: FINMA approves UBS's recovery plan for the first time since the Credit Suisse deal
stories.ticker: FINMA approves UBS recovery plan, first since Credit Suisse rescue; says bail-in strategy workable
stories.body:
FINMA has approved UBS's 2025 recovery plan, its first approval since the Credit Suisse takeover, and found the bank easier to resolve as the integration advanced; its preferred strategy, a bail-in to rebuild capital, can be carried out, FintechNews reports.

So what: it helps UBS argue against the tougher Swiss capital rules it is fighting.
stories.chip: Checked on FintechNews Switzerland (opened)
src: FintechNews CH: FINMA approves UBS recovery plan

stories.title: China publishes rules (27 Nov), issued by 11 departments including the PBoC and the Cyberspace Administration, for blockchain-based digital identities run on its national blockchain network, effective 1 March 2027
stories.h: China sets rules for blockchain digital IDs, effective March 2027
stories.ticker: China: blockchain-based digital ID rules from 11 agencies incl. PBoC take effect 1 Mar 2027
stories.body:
Eleven Chinese agencies including the People's Bank of China issued rules for blockchain-based digital identities on the national blockchain network, run by entities the cyberspace regulator authorises; they take effect on 1 March 2027, Cointelegraph reports.

So what: a state-run identity layer that banks and platforms in China will be expected to plug into for KYC.
stories.chip: Checked on Cointelegraph (opened)
src: Cointelegraph: China issues rules for blockchain-based digital identities

stories.title: A Spanish decree published 25 Nov would let the financial intelligence unit Sepblac freeze crypto accounts for up to five business days, and hold transactions up to ten, without a court order when it suspects money laundering; Congress must ratify within 30 days
stories.h: Spain moves to let its AML unit freeze crypto accounts without a judge
stories.ticker: Spain decree: Sepblac may freeze crypto accounts 5 days without court order
stories.body:
A decree published on 25 Nov would let Sepblac, Spain's financial intelligence unit, freeze crypto accounts for up to five business days and hold transactions for up to ten without prior judicial approval when it suspects money laundering or terrorist financing, Cointelegraph reports. Parliament must ratify it within 30 days.

So what: Spain's election on Sunday decides who votes on it.
stories.chip: Checked on Cointelegraph (opened)
src: Cointelegraph: Spain moves to allow crypto account freezes

stories.title: FIFA confirms (26 Nov, to AP) that cybercriminals accessed 'a limited set of personal and business information', a week after the Handsome Boy Hacking Club posted screenshots of what it said were FIFA files
stories.h: FIFA confirms hackers took personal and business data
stories.ticker: FIFA confirms breach of 'limited' personal and business data after hacker group posts files
stories.body:
FIFA told the AP that criminals got into its systems and took 'a limited set of personal and business information', and that it is working with law enforcement. A group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club had posted screenshots of alleged FIFA files a week earlier.

So what: with the 2030 World Cup planning under way, expect phishing that uses leaked FIFA data.
stories.chip: Checked on Help Net Security (opened), citing AP

stories.title: The FDA extends its review of Vertex's investigational kidney drug povetacicept (for IgA nephropathy) as the company faces questions about potential safety concerns, STAT reports (27 Nov)
stories.h: FDA extends its review of Vertex's kidney drug povetacicept
stories.ticker: FDA extends review of Vertex's povetacicept amid safety questions
stories.body:
The FDA is extending its assessment of Vertex's experimental kidney drug povetacicept, as the company faces questions about possible safety concerns, STAT reports.

So what: a delay for one of Vertex's main growth bets beyond cystic fibrosis.
stories.chip: Checked on STAT (opened; details behind STAT+)
src: STAT: FDA extends review of Vertex kidney drug

stories.h: Marc Márquez retires from MotoGP days after his eighth title
stories.ticker: Marc Márquez to retire after Valencia GP, days after record-equalling 8th title
stories.body:
Marc Márquez will retire after the Valencia Grand Prix this weekend, days after clinching an eighth premier-class title by overturning the biggest points deficit in MotoGP history, 102 points, the BBC reports. He topped Friday's practice.

So what: Ducati needs a new lead rider for 2027.
stories.chip: Checked on BBC Sport (opened)
src: BBC Sport: Marc Márquez to retire after final race of 2026

stories.title: Storms on both US coasts over Thanksgiving leave more than 360,000 households without power on Friday afternoon, Pennsylvania worst hit; New York and other states declare emergencies
stories.h: Thanksgiving storms leave 360,000 US homes without power
stories.ticker: US Thanksgiving storms: 360,000+ households without power Friday; Pennsylvania worst hit
stories.body:
Severe storms hit both US coasts during Thanksgiving; by Friday afternoon more than 360,000 households still had no power, with Pennsylvania worst hit, the BBC reports, citing Poweroutage.us. Parts of several states, including New York, declared emergencies; Macy's parade moved to Saturday.

So what: expect insured storm losses and a weaker read on holiday spending in the north-east.
stories.chip: Checked on BBC News (opened)
src: BBC: Hundreds of thousands still without power after Thanksgiving storms

stories.title: GTA 6 sold about 53 million copies in its first week after the 19 Nov launch, Alinea Analytics estimates (Polygon), against GTA 5's 29 million in its first month; nearly 7 million players have logged 50+ hours
stories.h: GTA 6 sold an estimated 53 million copies in its first week
stories.ticker: Alinea: GTA 6 ~53m copies in week one (GTA 5: 29m in first month)
stories.body:
Analytics firm Alinea estimates GTA 6 sold about 53 million copies in the week after its 19 Nov release, Polygon reports, against 29 million for GTA 5 in its whole first month; nearly 7 million players have already played more than 50 hours. Rockstar has not confirmed unit sales.

So what: Take-Two's numbers next quarter will be the biggest single-title result in entertainment.
stories.chip: Checked on Polygon (opened); figures are third-party estimates
src: Polygon: GTA 6 passes massive sales milestone

stories.title: A Kenyan court in Mombasa finds starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie guilty of manslaughter (27 Nov) for 123 deaths of followers at Shakahola; he is already serving a 200-year sentence for the murder of nearly 200 children
stories.h: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie convicted over 123 starvation deaths
stories.ticker: Kenya: Paul Mackenzie guilty of manslaughter for 123 Shakahola deaths
stories.body:
A court in Mombasa found Paul Mackenzie guilty of manslaughter for the deaths of 123 followers in the Shakahola forest; he is already serving 200 years for the murder of nearly 200 children, CNA (Reuters) reports.

So what: one of the deadliest cult cases in modern times moves toward a close.
stories.chip: Checked on CNA (opened)
src: CNA: Kenyan starvation cult leader guilty of manslaughter

stories.h: Villeneuve 'deeply disappointed' Avengers lands on Dune 3's weekend
stories.ticker: Dune: Part Three and Avengers: Doomsday both open 18 Dec
stories.body:
Director Denis Villeneuve told Deadline he is 'deeply disappointed' that Disney put Avengers: Doomsday on the same 18 December weekend as Dune: Part Three.

src: Deadline: Villeneuve 'deeply disappointed' by Avengers/Dune clash

stories.update: Bloomberg traces a banned GB300 rack to a Shanghai data centre tied to Megaspeed; FT says Nvidia halted South-East Asia shipments (Singapore calls that unconfirmed)
stories.title: Bloomberg reports (27 Nov) that Chinese loan filings show an Nvidia GB300-NVL72 rack, traced by serial number to Gigabyte, pledged as collateral for a 96m yuan ($14m) loan by Shanghai Shuoyao, a firm tied to Singapore's blacklisted Megaspeed, founded by Alice Huang; a second firm listed a GB200 server at the same site; the FT reports Nvidia halted chip shipments to South-East Asia, which Singapore calls unconfirmed while it seeks talks with the US to keep chip access; Nvidia closes up 0.8% at $150.49
stories.h: Banned Nvidia racks surface in Shanghai, tied to Alice Huang's Megaspeed, Bloomberg finds
stories.ticker: Bloomberg: banned GB300 rack pledged as loan collateral in Shanghai, linked to Megaspeed
stories.body:
Loan documents filed with Chinese regulators show a GB300-NVL72 rack, which may not be sold to China, pledged as collateral for a 96m yuan ($14m) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank to Shanghai Shuoyao, Bloomberg reports; it traced the rack through a serial number to Gigabyte. Bloomberg links Shuoyao to Megaspeed, the Singapore firm founded by Alice Huang that became Nvidia's biggest South-East Asian customer and was blacklisted by the US this month. The FT separately reported that Nvidia had halted chip shipments to South-East Asia; Singapore says that is unconfirmed and is in talks with Washington to keep access. Nvidia rose 0.8% to $150.49 on Friday; Jensen Huang faces House committee questions on 1 Dec.

So what: physical evidence of banned chips in China sharpens the export-control case against Nvidia's partner network, days before Huang's testimony.
stories.chip: Checked on The Decoder and SiliconANGLE (opened), both citing Bloomberg; FT halt report and Singapore response seen as headlines only
src: The Decoder: banned Nvidia Blackwell chips turn up in a Shanghai data centre (Bloomberg)
SiliconANGLE: report links Alice Huang to Chinese firms with smuggled Nvidia chips
The Information: Singapore in talks with US to keep AI chip access
Hacker News: Nvidia halts chip shipments to south-East Asia (FT)
stories.short: Bloomberg found a banned Nvidia GB300 rack pledged as loan collateral by a Shanghai firm tied to Megaspeed, the blacklisted Singapore partner founded by Alice Huang. The FT reported Nvidia halted shipments to South-East Asia; Singapore says that is unconfirmed. Jensen Huang faces House questions on 1 December.

stories.update: WSJ: the $35bn risk-weighted-asset booking error now triggers a shake-up in Citi's upper ranks
stories.title: Citigroup's roughly $35bn bookkeeping error (trades misbooked at a European trading unit, understating risk-weighted assets) sparks a shake-up in its upper ranks, the WSJ reports (28 Nov); details of who is moving were not available to us
stories.h: Citi's $35bn booking error leads to a management shake-up, WSJ says
stories.ticker: WSJ: Citi's $35bn risk-weighted-asset booking error sparks shake-up in upper ranks
stories.body:
The Wall Street Journal reports that Citigroup's $35bn bookkeeping error, trades misbooked at a European trading unit that understated its risk-weighted assets, has led to a shake-up in its upper ranks. We could only read the headline; names and roles are not confirmed here. Citi shares rose 2% to $115.59 on Friday.

So what: Citi is still under consent orders over data and risk controls, so another controls failure tests regulators' patience as it seeks to close them.
stories.chip: WSJ headline only (paywalled); not checked on an opened page
src: WSJ: Citigroup's $35 billion bookkeeping snafu sparks shake-up in upper ranks

stories.update: FT: UniCredit will propose CEO Andrea Orcel as Commerzbank chair
stories.title: UniCredit plans to propose its CEO Andrea Orcel as chair of Commerzbank, the FT reports (27 Nov), as it moves to take control of the German lender's board after reaching about 50% of voting rights and agreeing terms with Berlin
stories.h: UniCredit to put Orcel forward as Commerzbank chair, FT reports
stories.ticker: FT: UniCredit to propose Andrea Orcel as Commerzbank chair
stories.body:
UniCredit intends to propose its chief executive Andrea Orcel as chair of Commerzbank, the FT reports. UniCredit has close to half of Commerzbank's voting rights and said this month it would call a shareholder vote on a new board once it takes control; Reuters reported on 18-19 Nov that UniCredit and Berlin had settled the main sticking points. We could read only the FT headline.

So what: Orcel chairing the target would put Europe's biggest cross-border bank merger in years under one man's direct control.
stories.chip: FT headline only (paywalled); background from earlier opened reporting
src: FT: UniCredit to propose Orcel as chair of Commerzbank
